1. Open the starwars dataset (located in tidyverse)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("starwars")
```

2. Create a scatter plot of character's height and mass. 
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+geom_point()
```

2a. Change the color and shape of the points in your scatter plot. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+geom_point(color = "maroon",shape = 7)
```

3. Add Homeworld as a third variable to your scatterplot. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, colour = homeworld))+geom_point()
```

3a. What do you notice about the graph? (e.g. describe what you see)
#It is challenging to interpret because there are many levels for "homeworld" and our legend colors are hard to differentiate from each other.
4. Make a boxplot of height. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height))+geom_boxplot()
```

5. Make a boxplot of height for each species present in the data. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(species, height))+geom_boxplot()

```

5a. change the appearance of your graph in at least 3 ways. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(species, height))+geom_boxplot()+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))+geom_jitter(color="red", alpha = .3)+xlab("Species")+ylab("Height (cm)")+ggtitle("Height of Star Wars Characters by Species")
```

6. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from viridis.
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color=species))+geom_point()+scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "magma")
```

7.Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from RColorBrewer.
```{r}
library(RColorBrewer)
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color=sex))+geom_point()+scale_color_brewer(palette = "PuOr")
```

8. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph using facet_wrap
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, sex))+geom_boxplot()+facet_wrap(~hair_color)
```
```{r}
data("starwars")
```
